title: SignalOS Operator Manual
summary: Use drives, records, archives, racks, and apps as portable progression and information surfaces.

blocks.title: Overview
blocks.body: SignalOS turns data into an object you can hold, install, archive, and route through terminals. Drives are not junk if they carry records or boot behavior.

blocks.title: First Steps
blocks.body: Read drive labels, preserve unknown records, and install drives only where the terminal or rack expects them. Keep a clean backup when possible.

blocks.title: Core Loop
blocks.body: Recover drives, inspect records, install or archive them, use apps for context, and let discovered data point to the next route or system.

blocks.title: Important Systems
blocks.body: Drive templates, records, apps, archives, chapters, and missions can all add useful player-facing information, so check recovered drives before discarding them.

blocks.title: Integrations
blocks.body: Terminal hosts SignalOS surfaces, Wiki can summarize records, Index can expose data objects, and styled screens can make records easier to read when present.

blocks.title: Troubleshooting
blocks.body: If a drive appears empty, check its label, whether it has records, and whether the target block supports that drive role.
